description.narrative: Project Outcomes Stakeholder effects: (i) Effects on consumers: The Project entails supplying about 4,700 affordable housing units for sale in Abidjan, Cote DIvoire, thereby promoting increased access to affordable housing for the consumers; (ii) effects on local communities: The large-scale development is also expected to create potential economy-wide effects in the local community, creating demand for building materials, durable goods used for equipment and furnishing, and other relevant services in the area. Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: Project will demonstrate that good quality housing in the affordable segment can also be profitable; and can be replicable to serve the underserved population. The success of the Project can help alleviate the commercial risk perceived by banks and investors for affordable housing developments in Cote DIvoire, by demonstrating a strong case for the commercial viability of these projects, which will improve access to financing for the developers by crowding in more private capital into the sector. Through these demonstration effects, the Project will contribute to developing the depth and diversity of residential offerings in the market, thereby promoting competitiveness in the CI housing sector.

The proposed investment is a corporate A loan (the Loan) of up to EUR 25 million equivalent in local currency (XOF) in Douja Promotion - Groupe Addoha Cote DIvoire (Douja CIV or the Company), a leading housing developer in Cote DIvoire which primarily develops build-to-sell affordable housing units along with mid- to high-end housing in Cote DIvoire. The Company is a fully owned subsidiary of Groupe Addoha Douja Promotion (Addoha Group) a Moroccan real estate developer. The Loan will be used to partly finance the development of about 4,700 build-to-sell affordable housing units in the Companys project in Lagoona City.
